The four-sketch sequence is present, the construction views retain their vanishing rays and bounding crosses, and the bottom-right presentation view is your strongest piece — the roof pentagon, mid-body band, and base read as a coherent house form. That's real progress in spatial communication.

⚠️ Where to Pivot: Your two viewpoints are too similar in elevation angle and orientation, which means you're not yet extracting the full learning value from the two-viewpoint requirement. The assignment asks you to show the object from two genuinely different spatial positions — not two slight rotations of the same view. Additionally, your top-right presentation view still carries too much residual scaffolding; the 'clean contour' version should feel decisively different from the construction version, not just slightly darker. The line-weight contrast between construction and presentation needs to be more aggressive.

🛠️ Next Step: Redraw only the two presentation views — one from a low eye-level (near-worm's-eye, looking slightly up at the roof) and one from a high eye-level (bird's-eye, looking down at the roof plane). For each, use a two-pass method: first draw the full construction scaffold in very light lines, then overlay the final contour in a single confident, unbroken stroke per edge — no re-tracing, no feathering. The goal is that someone covering the construction sketch should see only a clean, readable house silhouette in the presentation view.
